items.title: Dipke to reach Delhi on Wednesday to join protest; CJP legal team to approach court over Tuesday detentions
items.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, speaking to media at his native village Santuk Pimpri (Hingoli, Maharashtra) where he attended his grandmother Savitribai Dipke's asthi visarjan, said he will reach Delhi on Wednesday to join the CJP protest demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation — and that if police stop him en route he will begin the agitation from wherever he is detained. He said CJP's legal team would approach the court over the Tuesday-morning detention of Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das after they unfurled the national flag at Jantar Mantar, adding he had spoken to his legal team from a car in Kundkar Pimpri village. He repeated that the agitation will continue until the CEC resigns and that 'the entire nation will turn Jantar Mantar'.

items.title: CJP policy lead Mehr Pasricha at press conference: 'everything is stealth at the moment, keep your eyes peeled'
items.summary: At CJP's latest press conference (ANI 'Top Moments' reel dated Oct 13), policy lead Mehr Pasricha recounted that after CJP met with the DCP he left quickly, and within 30 minutes a press release announced Jantar Mantar's de-notification — which she cast as proof the authorities are 'feeling the pressure'. She said CJP is 'not backing down' and that Jantar Mantar 'does not belong to any one man, two men who are making decisions'; next steps are undecided but 'everything is stealth at the moment, so keep your eyes peeled.'
